Easy.question: What is the difference between a list and a tuple in Python?
Easy.model_answer: A list is mutable, so its elements can be changed, added or removed after creation. A tuple is immutable, so it cannot be modified once created. Lists use square brackets and tuples use parentheses. Tuples are slightly faster and more memory efficient, and they can be used as dictionary keys when all their elements are hashable. Use a list for a collection that changes and a tuple for fixed data such as coordinates.

Easy.question: What is OOP? Name its four pillars.
Easy.model_answer: Object-Oriented Programming organizes software around objects that combine data and behavior. Its four pillars are encapsulation (bundling data with methods and hiding internal details), abstraction (exposing only essential features), inheritance (a child class reusing a parent class) and polymorphism (one interface with different behaviors). OOP makes code reusable, modular and easier to maintain.

Easy.question: What is the difference between a stack and a queue?
Easy.model_answer: A stack follows Last In First Out (LIFO): elements are pushed and popped from the same end. A queue follows First In First Out (FIFO): elements are enqueued at the rear and dequeued from the front. Stacks are used for undo features, function calls and expression evaluation. Queues are used for task scheduling, breadth-first search and buffering.

Easy.question: What is a variable and what are data types?
Easy.model_answer: A variable is a named location in memory that stores a value which can change during program execution. A data type defines what kind of value a variable holds and which operations are allowed on it. Common types are integer, float, string, boolean, list and dictionary. Python is dynamically typed, so the type is decided at runtime.

Easy.question: What is the difference between == and is in Python?
Easy.model_answer: The == operator compares values and checks whether two objects are equal. The is operator compares identity and checks whether two names refer to the same object in memory. For example, two separate lists with the same elements are equal with == but not identical with is. The is operator should be used mainly to compare with None.

Easy.question: What is version control and why is Git used?
Easy.model_answer: Version control is a system that tracks changes to files over time so you can view history, compare versions and revert mistakes. Git is a distributed version control system in which every developer has a full copy of the repository. It supports branching and merging, so teams can work in parallel and collaborate safely using commits, push, pull and pull requests.

Medium.question: Explain how a hash map works internally.
Medium.model_answer: A hash map stores key-value pairs in an array of buckets. A hash function converts the key into an integer, which is reduced to an array index. When two keys map to the same index it is called a collision, handled by chaining (a linked list per bucket) or open addressing (probing for the next free slot). When the load factor grows too high, the table is resized and rehashed. Average lookup, insert and delete take constant time.

Medium.question: What is the difference between REST and GraphQL?
Medium.model_answer: REST exposes multiple endpoints, one per resource, and uses HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT and DELETE. Each endpoint returns a fixed structure, which can cause over-fetching or under-fetching. GraphQL exposes a single endpoint where the client specifies exactly which fields it needs in a query, so it avoids both problems. REST is simpler and works well with HTTP caching, while GraphQL is more flexible but adds complexity.

Medium.question: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
Medium.model_answer: A process is an independent running program with its own memory space and resources. A thread is a lightweight unit of execution inside a process, and threads of the same process share its memory. Threads are cheaper to create and switch between, but shared memory requires synchronization such as locks to avoid race conditions. Processes are isolated, so a crash in one does not affect the others.

Medium.question: Explain how indexing speeds up a database query.
Medium.model_answer: An index is a separate data structure, usually a B-tree, that maps column values to the locations of rows. Without an index the database performs a full table scan and checks every row. With an index it can find rows in logarithmic time. The trade-off is extra storage and slower inserts, updates and deletes, because the index must also be maintained.

Medium.question: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL databases?
Medium.model_answer: SQL databases are relational: data lives in tables with a fixed schema, relationships are expressed with joins, and they provide strong ACID guarantees. NoSQL databases use flexible models such as document, key-value, column-family or graph, and they usually scale horizontally with eventual consistency. Choose SQL for structured, transactional data and NoSQL for large-scale, flexible or rapidly changing data.

Medium.question: Explain the SOLID principles briefly.
Medium.model_answer: SOLID is a set of five object-oriented design principles. Single Responsibility: a class should have one reason to change. Open/Closed: open for extension, closed for modification. Liskov Substitution: subclasses must be usable wherever the parent class is expected. Interface Segregation: prefer small specific interfaces over large ones. Dependency Inversion: depend on abstractions, not on concrete classes.

Hard.question: How would you design a URL shortener that handles millions of requests?
Hard.model_answer: Generate a unique short code for each long URL, for example by base62-encoding a unique ID from a distributed ID generator. Store the mapping in a database such as a key-value store, and when a user opens the short link, look it up and redirect with HTTP 301 or 302. Put a cache like Redis in front for popular links, use a load balancer with stateless servers, and shard or replicate the database for scale. Add rate limiting, link expiry and analytics as needed.

Hard.question: Explain deadlocks and how to prevent them.
Hard.model_answer: A deadlock occurs when two or more threads each hold a resource and wait for a resource held by another, so none can proceed. It requires four conditions: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait. Prevention means breaking at least one condition, for example by acquiring locks in a fixed global order, using lock timeouts or try-lock, avoiding nested locks, or detecting deadlocks and recovering.

Hard.question: How would you design a rate limiter for an API?
Hard.model_answer: Identify each client by API key, user ID or IP address and choose an algorithm such as token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window or sliding window. Store counters in a fast shared store like Redis using atomic operations with a time-to-live so the limit works across many servers. When the limit is exceeded, return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Place the limiter at the API gateway and make the limits configurable per client or endpoint.

Hard.question: Explain the CAP theorem with an example.
Hard.model_answer: The CAP theorem states that a distributed data store can guarantee only two of three properties: Consistency (every read sees the latest write), Availability (every request gets a response) and Partition tolerance (the system keeps working despite network failures). Since partitions cannot be avoided, the real choice is between consistency and availability during a partition. A banking system prefers consistency (CP), while a social media feed prefers availability (AP).

Hard.question: How would you design a real-time chat application?
Hard.model_answer: Use WebSockets for persistent two-way connections between clients and chat servers placed behind a load balancer. Route messages between servers with a message broker such as Redis Pub/Sub or Kafka. Store message history in a scalable database such as Cassandra, track user presence, send delivery and read receipts, and use push notifications for offline users. Keep servers stateless where possible and preserve message order within each conversation.

Hard.question: How do you find and fix a memory leak in a production application?
Hard.model_answer: First confirm the leak by monitoring memory usage over time and look for steady growth. Reproduce it in a test environment if possible, then capture heap dumps or profiler snapshots at different times and compare them to see which objects keep growing and what references retain them. Common causes are unbounded caches, unremoved listeners and global collections. Fix the cause by releasing references or bounding caches, deploy gradually, and add monitoring and regression tests.
